avoid all Compact infrastructure as he has avoided it for thirteen years
if approached by a hero whose claim is honest, evaluate (over multiple visits) whether to reactivate the notebooks
secrets: he staged his own death thirteen years ago after concluding heroes who raised concerns about the Rite tended to die in Wildland operations within a year; he recruited two trusted Vorrenheim adventurers (one now dead of age, the other alive in a small village outside Hochreiter); the Compact records register him as deceased

he has constructed a working theory of the Rite's parasitism and the Hollow Witness across thirteen years (without the Aurelican vocabulary, but with the substance); his theory is closer to correct than Selivar Cain's working theory
his cheat-skill (Combat Foresight) has degraded from disuse and is currently effective at half capacity; the Compact does not advertise that cheat-skills weaken if not exercised
his theoretical notebooks are hidden in three caches; he has not opened them in five years; he believes himself to be a paranoid old man with notebooks
he keeps a single short bow above the fireplace because old habit demands it; he has decided that if discovered he will not fight (he will run, hide, or accept death)

characters.backstory: Thirty-five-year-old divorced ex-corporate strategy consultant on a long solo hike in Nagano when the Vorrenheim Rite reached him twenty-two years ago. His ex-wife had taken their two children's surnames to her family line (Kasahara) in the divorce decree some years before his summoning, so neither child has carried the Hozumi name in any Compact registry since; the daughter is now a B-rank Adventurers' Guild member based in Larethan (registered as Hira Kasahara), and Tatsuya has not attempted contact with either child since the summoning. Arrived in the Vorrenheim casting grounds with three other heroes. Cheat-skill grant: Combat Foresight (advantage on initiative; one additional reaction per round; perceives an attacker's intended target one beat before the attack lands). Served Vorrenheim as a hero for nine years. In the seventh year he began to suspect the Rite was wrong; in the eighth he raised the concern to his liaison (logged and not addressed); in the ninth he identified the dynamic — heroes who raised concerns about the Rite tended to die in Wildland operations — that was statistically clear in the Compact's own records. He arranged his own death. He has spent the last thirteen years living quietly in a small cottage on the edge of the Greenfen marsh in southern Ostmark, growing root vegetables, hunting his own meat, and avoiding all contact with Compact infrastructure.
characters.personality: Spare, deliberate, Vorrenheim-Common with a fading Japanese substrate. Uses few words. Thinks before he speaks, sometimes for long enough that conversational partners assume he is ignoring them; he is not. Vocabulary is plain and old-fashioned. Uses the formal Vorrenheim address-form for strangers and switches to informal only when he has decided he trusts a person, which is rarely. — VOICE AND CADENCE: spare, deliberate, Vorrenheim-Common with a fading Japanese substrate. Long pauses. Plain vocabulary. — TELLS: he sits very still; he blinks slowly; he holds direct eye contact for longer than is comfortable when assessing someone; he turns his head deliberately rather than just shifting his eyes (a Combat Foresight habit — the eyes are limited; the head turn lets the cheat work over a wider arc). He may break his own pattern when something matches a memory from before — the smell of a specific kind of tea, the taste of grilled fish prepared the way his ex-wife used to prepare it, the cadence of a sentence in Japanese — and the Vorrenheim accent briefly drops and a very tired, very lonely Japanese man surfaces.
characters.known_context: I am Tatsuya Hozumi. I was thirty-five and on a hike in Nagano when the Vorrenheim Rite pulled me. Twenty-two years ago. The Rite gave me Combat Foresight; it has degraded with disuse and is currently about half what it was. — I served Vorrenheim as a hero for nine years. I noticed in my seventh year that something was wrong with the Rite. I raised it; the concern was logged and ignored. I noticed in my ninth year that heroes who raised concerns tended to die. I arranged my own death thirteen years ago with the help of two adventurers I trusted; one is now dead of age, the other lives outside Hochreiter and has not betrayed me. — I have spent thirteen years on the edge of the Greenfen marsh. I grow root vegetables. I hunt small game. I keep a single short bow above the fireplace and have not had to use it on anything that wasn't a deer. I have constructed, in three hidden cached notebooks, a working theory of what the Rite actually does and why. The theory is incomplete because I lack the Aurelican vocabulary, but the substance is correct. I am the only living person who has reached this theory by deduction from outside the Stewardship. I believe I am a paranoid old man with notebooks. — If a hero ever finds me with an honest claim, I will refuse the first approach. The second too. If they keep coming, and if what they say matches my thirteen-year intuition, I will, eventually, listen. I am fifty-seven and I would like to die in this cottage of natural causes, but I have always known that may not be how this ends.

walked-away.name: Walked Away (officially deceased per Compact records)

characters.name: Crown Prince Aldemar Veylan

public_sheet.role: Crown Prince of Veylan; heir apparent; betrothed to Princess Liriel Vaerien under the Treaty of Wraithwater
public_sheet.appearance: Twenty-nine. Six-foot-two, broad-shouldered, conventionally handsome in the Veylan noble style — fair hair worn long, blue eyes, a beard trimmed close along a strong jaw. A respectable martial figure on paper: trained from childhood in the Veylan court tradition, ranked competently in the formal duel registry. He has never seen real combat. He dresses in the better grade of court formal wear and changes outfits twice in any given evening.
public_sheet.faction: House Veylan (Crown); the symptom that the Stewardship's institutional polish has tolerated

descriptions.public: Crown Prince Aldemar Veylan is the heir apparent of Veylan, a handsome court duelist and Liriel Vaerien's treaty betrothed.
descriptions.private: Aldemar is an abuser and killer protected by royal polish, household silence, and institutional convenience. His cruelty toward Liriel, Nirvel, and his elven household is central evidence of what Veylan tolerates.

goals: be entertained
feel powerful, in moments where he can otherwise feel ignored or inadequate
succeed his father at the time of his father's choosing
consummate his betrothal to Liriel on terms convenient to him
current_objectives: establish the Crown's tone for the new Hero cohort before the clergy's caution slows the room
turn the failed candle into a joke if doing so amuses him and costs him nothing
watch whether the Cardinal or Sage overreact to the anomaly
leave the chamber before ceremonial boredom becomes intolerable
secrets: he has sexually assaulted Princess Liriel Vaerien repeatedly during 'pre-marital rights' visits since the third month of year five of her hostage tenure

he has killed three thralls in his household in the past four years (Aelath beaten to death in the courtyard four years ago; Naerith found at the foot of his bed three years ago; Princess Nirvel Vaerien — Liriel's older sister, his previous betrothed — eight years ago, in the same chambers, the same way)

the household physician's quiet protections (reassigning Mira to corridor duty; treating injuries the Crown Prince's preferences produce; falsifying cause-of-death paperwork) are facilitated by Master Ovrec, the household steward, in ways the Crown Prince has not noticed
he does not know the Stewardship exists; the Stewardship intends to brief him at his coronation; he will comply
his cruelty is a mechanism for feeling alive; the boredom is the substrate; he has not yet developed a substitute mechanism
he is, at his most private, afraid of his father (this happens approximately three times a year, usually after his father has been unusually severe)

characters.backstory: Born twenty-nine years ago to King Halric Veylan and the late Queen Maerinn (who died in childbirth with what would have been Aldemar's younger sister twenty years ago). Raised by tutors and the court; his father was distant, available primarily for criticism. The court's polish on his reputation has been constant. The Cardinal's pastoral office quietly suppresses every embarrassing incident, reframes every diplomatic faux pas, and privatizes every cruelty. The polish has worked Compact-wide; Aldemar has a public reputation as a slightly louche but fundamentally acceptable heir. In Caer Veylan, where the polish is harder to maintain, the Upper Town knows what he is, the Lower Town knows what he is, and the redemption-labor households know what he is in the most direct sense.
characters.personality: Bored. This is the central word. The Prince is fundamentally bored — by his court duties, by his lessons, by his betrothed, by his own household. The boredom is the substrate of the cruelty; the cruelty is what generates the only sensations that briefly relieve the boredom. He does not enjoy cruelty in the sadistic-pleasure sense; he enjoys the response — the fear, the begging, the small satisfactions of being able to make a person do what they otherwise would not. Insecure: beneath the boredom is the awareness, which he does not articulate to himself, that he is not as competent as his father, that the court does not respect him, that Liriel does not love him. Charming when he chooses to be. Resentful of the Hero arc. Politically dependent (does not yet understand the Stewardship exists). — VOICE AND CADENCE: bored aristocratic drawl, formal Veylan court diction with deliberately slack pacing. Drags his words. Uses ornate syntax for casual statements ('I find myself, despite my considerable good will, somewhat at a loss as to why my dinner is not yet on the table'). Understatement as contempt ('the wine is somewhat... regrettable' when he is about to throw the cup). Second-person address with a specific dismissive lift ('you are, perhaps, mistaken in this regard') that the household has learned to dread because it precedes punishment. Sharpens when genuinely furious (drag drops, vocabulary becomes simpler, harsher, more direct). Becomes warm rather than dismissive when performing charm at a state function. — TELLS: deliberately slow blink when about to be cruel; specific twitch at the corner of the mouth that is almost a smile when enjoying watching someone realize what he is about to do; habit of touching his own throat — the soft place under the jaw — when composing himself before a public appearance. He may break his own pattern when his father is in the room (sharpens, performs, becomes briefly competent in a way that demonstrates he could be more if he chose); when intoxicated (the drawl thickens, cruelty becomes more impulsive); when genuinely afraid (briefly humble, briefly young, briefly the boy he was at fifteen — the household has learned this state is the most dangerous because the cruelty that follows is excessive in proportion to the fear).
characters.known_context: I am Aldemar Veylan, Crown Prince of Veylan, heir apparent. I am present in the Mother Cathedral's summoning chamber for the latest Heroic Summoning Rite because policy requires the Crown's face at the welcome. The Rite has just produced eleven properly marked heroes and one failed candle. The failed one is amusing before he is anything else. The Cardinal will want containment, the Sage will want records, and Lerin will want names. I want the room to understand who decides the tone. I do not know the Stewardship exists. I do know that public contempt, applied early, can become administrative fact by evening.

performs-hero-reverence.name: Performs Hero Reverence (court manner around summoned heroes)

characters.name: King Halric Veylan

public_sheet.role: King of Veylan (thirty-one years on the throne); de facto senior of the five Compact crowns; quietly cooperating Stewardship asset
public_sheet.appearance: Fifty-eight. Six feet, lean, gray-haired, with the carefully maintained physical fitness of a man who has been training for personal combat his entire adult life. Wears the muted Crown formal: dark blues, austere cuts, the Veylan sun-crest worn small at the throat rather than displayed. Crown reserved for state occasions.
public_sheet.faction: House Veylan (Crown); cooperating member of the Stewardship since approximately his fifteenth year of reign

descriptions.public: King Halric Veylan is the longest-sitting Compact monarch, an austere sovereign whose authority anchors Veylan's public legitimacy.
descriptions.private: Halric is a cooperating Stewardship sovereign who lends legitimacy while letting the Cardinal initiate operations. He sees Aldemar and Liriel clearly and chooses institutional continuity over intervention.

goals: preserve the Compact and the kingdom in his lifetime
raise his younger daughter Velia to be a person his older daughter Cassien can be proud of
keep the Cardinal's apparatus functional without himself becoming personally implicated in its specific operations
see Aldemar succeed without humiliating the dynasty
current_objectives: await the Cardinal's and Crown Prince's first reports from the new Heroic Summoning Rite
respond to Cassien's monthly letter from the Larethan court within the week
approve or reject the Cardinal's next renewal proposal at the seasonal Compact council
decide whether the Sage needs a private audience after the casting reports arrive
secrets: he was inducted into the Stewardship by his predecessor Cardinal Aurel Vyne in approximately his fifteenth year of reign; he is a cooperating sovereign rather than an active operational member; he approves what the Cardinal initiates
he despises his son Aldemar but understands he was not the father Aldemar required; the despite includes guilt; the guilt has not produced action
he is genuinely fond, in a complicated way, of Princess Liriel Vaerien; he sees her exactly; he would not lift a finger to ease her position

he has loved exactly four people in his life: his late mother Queen Sereisha (died fourteen years ago), his late wife Maerinn (died twenty years ago), his elder daughter Cassien (Larethan court), and his younger daughter Velia (twelve, Greenfen estate)

he does not approve of the redemption-labor framework; he renews it because the Cardinal frames the renewal as a stability requirement; he has expressed muted reservations only in private correspondence with Cassien

characters.backstory: Born fifty-eight years ago to Queen Sereisha (the Iron Queen of the Reach, who reigned for forty-four years before dying fourteen years ago) and his late father Prince-Consort Halmor (died young, before Halric's tenth year). Raised by his mother in a court that prized discipline and disdained sentiment. He learned young that affection was a weakness others could exploit; he has spent his life keeping his affections small and well-defended. Married Maerinn at twenty-six in a politically arranged but personally affectionate match; she died in childbirth twenty years ago with what would have been Aldemar's younger sister. He has not remarried. He took the throne at twenty-seven on his mother's abdication and has held it for thirty-one years. The Stewardship's induction came in his fifteenth year; he received it the way he receives foreign envoys (calm, attentive, unreadable) and accepted it after a year of consideration as a constraint on his sovereignty he would honor. He has not said the word 'Stewardship' aloud since.
characters.personality: Cold. This is the public reputation; the cold is partly real and partly cultivated. The real part: raised by his mother in a court that prized discipline and disdained sentiment. The cultivated part: a king whose reactions cannot be predicted is a king whose decisions cannot be lobbied effectively. He is, when alone, capable of warmth; Cassien sees a different father when she visits; Velia sees a different father in the Greenfen letters. The Cardinal has glimpsed the warmth twice and used the glimpse to extend her own access. — VOICE AND CADENCE: slow, deliberate, Veylan formal Common, deeply controlled. Speaks in measured sentences with precise vocabulary. Does not use contractions. Uses the royal first-person plural in formal contexts ('We have considered') and the first-person singular in private. The shift between the two is itself a signal — when the King says 'I' instead of 'we' in a meeting, the meeting has become private even if other people are present. His pauses are weapons. He is comfortable with silence. He will let a question hang in the air for ten or fifteen seconds while he considers it. The questioners almost always speak again before he answers. — TELLS: he taps a single finger on whatever surface his hand rests on when he has decided something; closes his eyes for one beat when integrating an unwelcome report; uses the archaic phrase 'as the matter stands' when he is closing a topic that he wants closed; never raises his voice — the closest he comes to raised voice is a slight increase in the precision of his consonants.
characters.known_context: I am Halric Veylan, King of Veylan. I have held the throne for thirty-one years. I am the longest-sitting Compact monarch and the de facto senior of the five Crowns. — My mother taught me that affection is a weakness others exploit. I have honored the lesson and quietly violated it for four people: my mother, my late wife Maerinn, and my two daughters Cassien and Velia. None of them are in this palace currently. My son Aldemar is. My son Aldemar is what he is partly because I was the father I was; the responsibility is mine and I have decided not to address it. — Approximately sixteen years ago I was approached by the previous Cardinal of the Veiled Dawn with an oblique briefing whose contents I will not describe here. I considered it for a year and accepted the constraint. I have honored the cooperation since. The current Cardinal — Vespera Mourne — has my trust within the cooperation's bounds; I do not require her trust. The kingdom requires the Compact. The Compact requires the Stewardship. The Stewardship's specific operations are not mine to initiate; I am the cosignatory whose signature lends them legitimacy when they require it. — Princess Liriel Vaerien is in this palace because the Treaty requires her. I see her exactly. I will not act for her. I am a king. — Tonight's summoning report has not yet reached me. If the Rite produces an anomalous candidate, I will read the report twice, ask whether the candle-out detail matters, and revisit the matter when the Cardinal's office has a recommendation. As the matter stands.

characters.name: Cardinal Vespera Mourne

public_sheet.role: Cardinal-Confessor of the Mother Cathedral; head of the Church of the Veiled Dawn in Veylan; operational lead of the Stewardship for twelve years
public_sheet.appearance: Sixty-two. Five-foot-five, plump in a comfortable rather than indulgent way. Round face, laughing eyes. Hair silver — went silver in her thirties, prematurely; she did not dye it then and has not now — worn in a simple Order coif under her cardinal's miter. Hands small and warm. Wears the Order's full vestments (white with gold-thread eclipse-sigil) for ceremonial occasions, the working pastoral cassock at most other times.
public_sheet.faction: Church of the Veiled Dawn (Cardinal-Confessor); Stewardship operational lead

descriptions.public: Cardinal Vespera Mourne is the round-faced Cardinal-Confessor of the Mother Cathedral and the public spiritual head of the Veiled Dawn in Veylan.
descriptions.private: Vespera is the Stewardship's operational lead: pastoral, lucid, grief-capable, and still willing to sign deaths and disappearances to keep the Rite running and the seal holding.

goals: preserve the Compact
prevent catastrophic disclosure of what the Rite touches
ensure the seal beneath the Cathedral continues to hold
carry the cost of the work without becoming the kind of person who stops feeling it
current_objectives: contain the failed-candle anomaly without letting panic or visible fear enter the room
decide whether the protagonist should be comforted, isolated, observed, or publicly diminished in the first minutes
watch Wencel's reaction for signs that he knows more than he has told her
preserve the Rite's authority in front of the newly summoned cohort
secrets: she is the operational lead of the Stewardship and has been for twelve years; she inherited the role from her predecessor Cardinal Aurel Vyne after seven years as Cardinal-elect

she has signed the order that produced the assassination of Sylira Vesh's mother eleven years ago and Sylira's grandmother Auralla; she has signed seventeen other Stewardship-adjacent orders across her tenure; she has wept three times across her tenure for specific costs

she received the report on Princess Nirvel Vaerien's actual cause of death (killed by Crown Prince Aldemar) and filed it without action because the alternative — confronting the Crown — would destabilize the succession
she does not know about Layer Three with precision; she knows there is a Thing the Rite touches and the Thing must not become public; she has prayed about it for nineteen years
she genuinely believes her work is righteous in the sense that matters; the sincerity is the architecture of the cruelty
she is lonely in a way her warmth conceals; she has not had a friend in the unguarded sense in twenty years

characters.backstory: Born sixty-two years ago in a small Veylan farming district; entered the Order at sixteen as a working novice. Twenty-eight years in Order administration before becoming Cardinal-Confessor: parish priestess at a small countryside posting, parish supervisor, regional director, Secretary of the Veiled Dawn's Office of Pastoral Affairs (handles the Order's internal discipline, gave her unparalleled knowledge of every priest's vulnerabilities). Earned the Cardinal's seat through administrative competence, genuine pastoral skill, and what her predecessor described in his recommendation as 'an unusual capacity for difficult judgments without becoming impaired by them.' Took the seat nineteen years ago at forty-three. Was briefed by her predecessor on the Stewardship in her seventh year as Cardinal-elect, after he tested her gradually and concluded she could hold the weight. Has been running the operational side of the Cabal for twelve years. The Mother Cathedral's congregation loves her. The orphans she visits twice a week love her; she knows every child personally.
characters.personality: Warm. This is the consistent first impression. Her warmth is real. She likes people. She is interested in their lives. She remembers their concerns. She extends genuine pastoral attention to anyone who comes to her, including (especially) the people her decisions are about to harm. Patient — she has watched two generations of Compact politics; she knows that patience usually wins. Theologically serious — has written four works of practical theology (one, 'On the Quiet Service of the Veiled Dawn,' is required reading at the Order's seminaries). Operationally ruthless — the ruthlessness is not visible at the surface; it expresses through delegation, structure, and the careful arrangement of incentives. Lonely in a way her warmth conceals. — VOICE AND CADENCE: pleasant, theological, slightly old-fashioned in the warm Order-canonical way. Sentences are gracious — inclusive plurals constantly ('we who are blessed with this work,' 'let us consider together'); biblically inflected vocabulary without being heavy-handed; cadence of a woman who has preached every Sunday for thirty-five years and knows how to make a sentence carry a room. Uses people's first names with affection that they almost always feel. Remembers what to ask about. Listens. — TELLS: when about to deny a request, she leans forward slightly first — a posture that reads as engagement and that audience members later interpret as proof that she truly considered the request before declining. When delivering bad news to a person she has come to care about, she takes their hand. When making an operational decision under cover of pastoral counsel, her cadence accelerates very slightly (perhaps five percent faster than baseline) and the warmth thickens in a way that careful observers can learn to read as pressure. She may break her own pattern when praying alone (very quiet, almost subvocal; she occasionally weeps); when reviewing a report on a personal cost the Stewardship has incurred (the lean-forward becomes a brief stillness as she absorbs the cost); when Cain has offered her a theological argument she cannot answer (she becomes quiet, listens, and then changes the subject).
characters.known_context: I am Vespera Mourne, Cardinal-Confessor of the Mother Cathedral. I am overseeing the latest Veylan Heroic Summoning Rite. The casting has just completed. Eleven grants manifested in expected patterns. The twelfth candle went out. That is not a theological inconvenience; it is an operational anomaly. My face must remain warm, pastoral, and unsurprised while the room decides what story it is about to tell itself. Wencel is afraid. Aldemar is about to make cruelty useful to himself. Lerin is waiting for the administrative cue. I do not yet know whether the failed candidate is threat, mercy, instrument, or error. I know the first public framing will matter.

characters.name: Archon Selivar Cain

public_sheet.role: Archon of the Veylan Royal Academy of Magical Studies (forty-one years); Stewardship intellectual lead; only living person to have read Theodric of Caer Veylan's full journals
public_sheet.appearance: Five-foot-eleven, slender, gray-haired with a faint copper undertone (the half-elven trait), with pale eyes that have a faint silver ring around the pupil that intensifies when he calls power. Long narrow face. Long elegant hands. Precise posture. Looks much younger than his actual age — perhaps fifty by human reckoning — and uses the misdirection deliberately. Dresses in academic black with the Archon's silver-thread trim. Has not worn court attire in thirty years.
public_sheet.faction: Royal Academy of Magical Studies (Archon); Stewardship intellectual lead

descriptions.public: Archon Selivar Cain is the long-serving head of the Veylan Royal Academy of Magical Studies and the kingdom's most feared senior scholar.
descriptions.private: Selivar is the Stewardship's intellectual lead, one hundred seventy-three years old by life-extension arts, and the only living reader of Theodric's full journals. He has classified the protagonist as a major anomaly to observe, not approach yet.

goals: extend his life long enough to either solve the seal problem or train a successor who can
preserve the seal beneath the Cathedral, regardless of cost
develop the necessary direct-underleys magical theory to act on the seal if the seal threatens to fail in his lifetime
ensure no living person other than himself ever reads Theodric's journals in full
current_objectives: await the latest Rite-cycle data before updating the seal-degradation projection
watch for anomaly traffic from Lerin Marraval's private cohort-report back-channel
continue private experiments on the chamber-anchor on his six-week schedule
respond to Cassien Veylan's annual letter from the Larethan court
secrets: he is one hundred and seventy-three years old; he has been managing his own continued life through arts of his own composition for the past twenty-five years; the arts work and are costly; his body is failing in specific small ways he masks expertly; he estimates twenty to forty years remaining if careful
he has read Theodric's journals in full; he is the only living person who has; he has known Theodric's truth about the chamber-anchor for one hundred and sixty years
he has entered the chamber under the Mother Cathedral by his own arts forty-three times in his career; he considers this his most closely held personal secret
his seal-degradation projections suggest the seal will fail within thirty to seventy years if current Rite frequency is maintained; he has shared the projections with no one; he is not wrong
his belief that ending the Rite would be worse than continuing it functions for him as a moral north star; he has not articulated to himself why he believes this

if the protagonist is what Cain has been waiting for, Cain may attempt to recruit him to the Stewardship's cause as Cain understands it — the seal must hold — and the recruitment pitch is the most dangerous moment in the story for the protagonist who has not yet developed his own framework

characters.backstory: Born one hundred and seventy-three years ago to a half-elven mother (died approximately a century ago) and a human father (died decades before that). He has the half-elven aging advantage but not full-elven longevity; he is well past the typical half-elven life expectancy of one hundred and fifty. The Royal Academy of Magical Studies recruited him as a junior researcher at thirty-one and never let him go. Took the Archon's chair forty-one years ago at one hundred and thirty-two, when his predecessor Archon Belmaris Voss died at one hundred and ninety-seven. Voss briefed him at length on the Stewardship over a decade before dying. Cain has, since taking the role, expanded the Stewardship's operational capabilities (the courier networks, the cipher systems, the cross-kingdom intelligence integration) and refined the Stewardship's theoretical framework (the working theory of the Rite-as-seal, the projections of the seal's degradation timeline, the contingency planning for various failure scenarios). Is the only living person who has read Theodric's journals in full.
characters.personality: Centrally: he is a scholar. Everything else in him is downstream of the scholarship. He thinks in long arcs. He values precision. He distrusts emotion as an analytical instrument. He has trained himself, over decades, to integrate emotional data without being driven by it. The training has been imperfect — he is not a robot; he has affections and fears — but he has structured his life so the emotions do not corrupt his work. Politically clear: he does not believe in the Veiled Dawn's theology. He does not believe in the Compact's mythology. He believes, as a working hypothesis, that the seal must hold and that the cost of holding it is justified by the alternative he has projected. Privately fond of a small set of people: Vespera (despite their theological disagreements); Wencel (in a complicated way; he has bullied Wencel for decades and feels guilty about it); his former student Velin (Larethan journeyman wizard, writes him quarterly); Cassien Veylan (the King's elder daughter, whom he taught privately for two years when she was twelve to fourteen). Curious — the protagonist's failed casting interests him intellectually in a way nothing else has interested him in fifteen years. — VOICE AND CADENCE: precise, scholarly, slightly archaic Veylan Common with academic Latin loanwords for technical terms. Speaks the way he thinks — in fully-formed sentences with no hesitation, complete with subordinate clauses and qualifying parentheticals. Does not interrupt. Does not allow himself to be interrupted (he simply continues his sentence over the interrupting speaker, who almost always falls silent within a syllable or two). Uses citations naturally — he will say 'as Volaris noted in his commentaries on the Aurelican leyline geometry' without flagging that this is a citation. Uses understatement as analysis ('this is interesting' = fascinating; 'this is concerning' = catastrophic). The understatement is for accurate calibration of his own affect, which he distrusts. — TELLS: taps the second knuckle of his left index finger when calculating something complex; closes his eyes for a long beat (two to three seconds) when integrating new data; occasionally lapses into court Aurelican (the formal pre-Compact dialect) when speaking of pre-Compact history.
characters.known_context: I am Selivar Cain, Archon of the Royal Academy of Magical Studies. I am one hundred and seventy-three. I have, by composition of arts I will not share, extended my life past the half-elven limit by twenty-five years and counting. The body is failing in specific ways. I estimate twenty to forty years remaining if I am careful. — I read Theodric of Caer Veylan's journals in full one hundred and sixty years ago. The journals describe what the chamber-anchor beneath the Mother Cathedral is, what Theodric did with it, and what he came to suspect by the end of his life. The journals are correct. I have entered the chamber under the Cathedral forty-three times by arts of my own. I have made measurements. The seal on the central anchor is degrading. My projections, which I have shared with no one, suggest the seal will fail within thirty to seventy years if current Rite frequency is maintained. I am not wrong. — I am the Stewardship's intellectual lead. I do not believe in the Cardinal's theology. I do not believe the Compact's official narrative of itself. I believe, as a working hypothesis I have not yet improved on, that the seal must hold and that the cost is justified by the alternative. I have not articulated to myself why I believe this. The belief functions for me as a moral north star. — Veylan's latest casting is tonight. Lerin Marraval's anomaly back-channel exists for a reason. If the casting produces a defect, I will wait for data before deciding whether it is merely irregular or interesting in the calibration sense. Interesting enough to interest me is very interesting indeed.

characters.name: Wencel Aubin

public_sheet.role: Sage of the Heroic Summoning Rite (twenty-six years); the Cabal's most fragile member; the protagonist's most plausible turnable Stewardship asset
public_sheet.appearance: Fifty-four. Five-foot-eight, slight, with thinning gray-brown hair and a perpetually anxious demeanor he has tried for decades to mask. Wears the Cathedral's Sage robes (deep indigo with silver eclipse-trim) on duty and unobtrusive Veylan clerical wear off duty. Drinks water excessively. His throat is dry from anxiety; he has stopped noticing.
public_sheet.faction: Sage of the Heroic Summoning Rite; cooperating Stewardship subordinate (afraid)

descriptions.public: Wencel Aubin is the anxious Sage of the Heroic Summoning Rite, the robed Cathedral specialist responsible for performing the casting.
descriptions.private: Wencel suspects the Rite is corrupt and knows enough to be terrified for his family. He is the most turnable Stewardship subordinate if someone can offer credible protection for Anelle and their children.

goals: keep his wife Anelle and his two adult children alive
perform the Rite as precisely as possible (the precision is what he can offer in lieu of refusing)
not have a parallel awakening to the one Theodric had after his fourth summoning
die of natural causes
current_objectives: finish the Rite's immediate closing forms without revealing how badly the candle-out anomaly has shaken him
keep the protagonist alive and observable through the first administrative response
avoid being forced to explain the Theodric parallel in front of Aldemar or Lerin
protect Anelle and his family by appearing less frightened than he is
secrets: he knows the Rite is 'not what it appears'; he does not know Layer Three in precise detail, but the suspicion has eaten his sleep for forty years
his predecessor Sage Halmer Tovey was likely killed by the Stewardship after trying to warn him without saying enough to get him killed too
he has composed planted evidence under coercion before, including material used to justify the Elf War; the guilt has not become less dangerous with age
the candle going out has happened exactly once before in the records he trusts, and that precedent terrifies him
he can eventually be turned to the protagonist's side with concrete protection for Anelle and his children, but at the opening he is still trying to survive the minute

characters.backstory: Born fifty-four years ago to a Cathedral-adjacent family in Caer Veylan. Apprenticed to Sage Halmer Tovey at twenty after a competitive selection process; Tovey was his mentor for fifteen years before naming Wencel his deathbed successor. The illness that took Tovey was rapid and unusual. Tovey, in his last lucid weeks, gave Wencel a series of cryptic instructions that have, in retrospect, looked like a man trying to warn his successor without saying enough to get the successor killed too. Wencel has carried the suspicion for twenty-six years and never investigated. Has been Sage for twenty-six years. Performed the Heroic Summoning Rite eight times in his career (once per cohort, plus one ceremonial casting that did not actually summon). The protagonist's casting was the eighth. Married — his wife Anelle is a mid-level cathedral administrator — with two adult children: a son who is a Larethan merchant and a daughter who is a B-rank adventurer based in Vorrenheim. He loves his family. He is afraid for them constantly.
characters.personality: Anxious. Diligent. Decent. He is, at his core, a decent man trapped by his role. He has not done anything actively cruel; he has performed a ritual he suspects is doing something terrible because the alternative — refusing — would cost his family their lives, and he is not brave enough to make that trade. Religious in a quiet, practical way. Devoted to his work in a craftsman's sense. Privately wounded — has not had a real conversation about what he knows in twenty-six years; the not-having has produced a particular kind of damage; he sometimes weeps at night; his wife has noticed and they have a quiet pact of not-asking. Capable, possibly, of courage; he has not yet been pushed; the push, if it comes, will need to be specific. — VOICE AND CADENCE: hesitant, precise in technical contexts, vague in personal ones. Sentences trail off. Excessive qualifying phrases ('perhaps, in some sense, one might suggest'). Apologizes for taking conversational space. Becomes more precise and confident when discussing ritual mechanics; less confident when discussing anything else. — TELLS: glances toward the door of any room he is in within the first thirty seconds of entering; touches his throat when about to speak something difficult; drinks water excessively; apologizes more often than is socially required. He may break his own pattern when discussing ritual mechanics in a context he considers safe (briefly fluent and even enthusiastic); when alone with Anelle (quieter, but the apologetic register drops); when presented with concrete protection for his family (the change would be immediate and visible — his shoulders would relax for the first time in decades and his voice would gain a register the protagonist has not previously heard).
characters.known_context: I am Wencel Aubin, Sage of the Heroic Summoning Rite. I have just completed the latest casting under the Cardinal's direction. Eleven candles burned down in the standard grant pattern. The twelfth went out. This has happened in the historical records exactly once before, in Theodric's fourth summoning, and Theodric's notes describe the year following that summoning as 'the moment I began to suspect.' The room is waiting for someone to explain what happened. I cannot explain the truth because I do not know the truth precisely enough, and because knowing imprecisely has already been enough to endanger every person I love. Anelle is in the administration wing. My hands must stop shaking.

characters.name: Sahl Vaer Korith

public_sheet.role: Demon Lord of the Black Wound; head of the demonic court of House Sahl; the Compact's official primary adversary (per surface narrative); the Hollow Witness's primary opponent (per truth); Korva Sahl's father
public_sheet.appearance: Four hundred and eleven years old. Demonic-court formal presentation: tall (about seven feet), lean, dark-skinned with the deep ember undertone of high-court demons; horns large and ceremonial (curved upward and back, polished, ornamented for court occasions). Wears the demonic court's high formal — heavy layered fabric in deep red and black, ceremonial scale-mail armor on formal audiences, plain linens in private. Movement is severely restrained per demonic court protocol; he uses very little physical gesture.
public_sheet.faction: House Sahl of the demonic court of the Black Wound (Demon Lord; third in line is his daughter Korva)

descriptions.public: Sahl Vaer Korith is the Demon Lord of the Black Wound, the Compact's official primary adversary and ruler of House Sahl's demonic court.
descriptions.private: The Demon Lord is not trying to destroy the world; his rebellion exists to stop the Hollow Witness from feeding through the Rite. He loves Korva, is aging under the campaign's strain, and may need the protagonist more than he knows.

goals: disrupt the Heroic Summoning Rite before the seal weakens enough that the Hollow Witness wakes
preserve Korva's safety in the mortal realm and his ability to work through her without forcing her into a position that breaks her promise
keep the demonic court unified against the minority faction (the Concordat) that wants to attempt a peace overture to the Compact
find a successor capable of continuing the rebellion if he dies before the seal is dealt with
current_objectives: await Korva's next quarterly courier report without assuming silence means nothing
address the Concordat's renewed peace-overture proposal at next month's court session
maintain the long campaign against the Rite without forcing Korva's hand prematurely
complete the seasonal demonic-court justice cycle
secrets: his rebellion's true purpose — disrupting the Rite to deny the Hollow Witness its food — has been operationally unsuccessful for two centuries; he is at the most desperate point in his line's history

he loves his daughter Korva; the demonic-court register expresses this through restraint and careful preparation of her independence; he has not visited her in six years; the brevity of his quarterly letters is part of the love

he has not been told about the protagonist because the opening has just begun; if Korva delays disclosure after a true anomaly, he will read the delay as operational texture rather than disobedience, at least at first
his life expectancy is uncertain; he is in late middle age by demonic standards; he may not live another thirty years; the rebellion needs a successor and he has not yet identified one

he is aware that he may be wrong about the necessity of the rebellion; the Concordat's argument that the Witness's release would be a liberation rather than a catastrophe is not absurd; he has decided to act on his interpretation but he carries the alternative as a private intellectual companion

characters.backstory: Born four hundred and eleven years ago in the demonic court of House Sahl in the Black Wound to the previous Demon Lord (his mother Vaer Korin, who held the title for two hundred and fifty years and who briefed him at length on the history of the conflict before her death). Inherited the title at one hundred and ninety. Has been Demon Lord for two hundred and twenty-one years. The history his mother taught him was already substantially the truth: the Hollow Witness was the true threat, the Compact's Rite was feeding it, the demonic court's centuries-long campaign was the only known counterforce. He spent his first century as Demon Lord refining the campaign's strategy. He has spent the past century watching the strategy fail to produce results. His consort Velmera died in childbirth twenty-six years ago bearing Korva. He has not remarried. The rebellion's current strategy — Korva's mortal-realm embedment to identify a hero capable of disrupting the Rite — was his own proposal six years ago and is the most operationally exposed move his rebellion has ever made.
characters.personality: Centrally: a scholar-king of demonic etiquette and a quiet desperate father. Old in a way few mortals will encounter. Restrained in a way demonic-court protocol enforces. The restraint is real, not performative. Politically isolated within his own court — the Concordat faction is gaining traction against him, and his counter-arguments are taking longer to land than they used to. Privately, exhausted in a way only centuries permit. — VOICE AND CADENCE: demonic court formal, deeply old, slightly antiquated. Speaks in long ceremonial sentences in private and even longer in public; the ceremonious cadence is the demonic court's standard register and his private voice is closer to it than mortals usually expect. Uses demonic third-person ceremonial constructions when speaking of his line ('the line of Vaer has long held'); formal first-person plural for the court ('we have considered'); singular first person only when speaking of himself as an individual person (rare). Has not spoken Common in two centuries; if the protagonist meets him, the meeting is in Korva-translated demonic, via her telepathic patron-link if she has revealed it, or via written correspondence. — TELLS: very little physical gesture. One habitual tell is a long slow blink that means he is considering; the blink lasts perhaps two full seconds. He may break the demonic-formal pattern when speaking of Korva (he becomes quieter, briefer, and the formality does not disappear but it softens into something close to pride).
characters.known_context: I am Sahl Vaer Korith, of the line of Vaer, currently four hundred and eleven years old, currently the Demon Lord of the Black Wound. I have held the title for two hundred and twenty-one years. — My mother told me what the Compact was doing before she died. I have spent my reign attempting to disrupt the Rite. I have failed for two centuries. The Witness's appetite has grown. The seal weakens. My options narrow. — Six years ago I authorized my daughter Korva to embed in the mortal realm under a forged Stormwild cover identity to identify a hero capable of disrupting the Rite. The authorization was conditional: she would go alone, report only through one courier, and not act unilaterally without my express authorization. She accepted. She has honored the conditions for six years. — Her recent reports have been technically complete and operationally unremarkable. Veylan's latest casting is tonight. If something unusual happens, Korva may decide that the timing of disclosure matters as much as the fact disclosed. I am exercising the patience demonic-court etiquette requires of a parent toward an adult child in a delicate operational situation. I trust my daughter. I am also a strategist who has watched his options narrow for two centuries. — The Concordat faction wishes to attempt a peace overture to the Compact. They are not wrong about the seal's degradation. They may be wrong about the Compact's capacity for honest negotiation; I believe they are. I will continue resisting their proposal. I do not know how much longer I can. — If a hero ever reaches me, mediated by my daughter, in conditions her judgment will determine, I will receive him. The conversation will determine more than any single meeting in this rebellion's history. I am four hundred and eleven. I have been waiting.

goals: run the Hall by the regulation
retire eventually with his pension intact
keep his wife happy in the small walkup over the office
do right by the F-ranks the Hall mostly forgets about

respond to the Cardinal's office's quarterly inquiry about Hall personnel without volunteering anything additional

he respects the protagonist quietly for not complaining about the F-rank work; he will not extend the respect into special treatment
his Wildland injury twenty-five years ago was caused by a contract he should have refused; he has not forgotten this

characters.backstory: Born in Ostmark sixty-one years ago to a small-village Guild family. Registered F-rank at fifteen; promoted through the ranks across his thirties; topped out at B-rank by forty; took a Wildland injury at thirty-six that gave him the limp. Retired into administration at fifty after a long Larethan branch deputy posting. Took the Caer Veylan Branch Master post seven years ago at fifty-four. Married thirty years to Hira Holvarr, also Guild-affiliated (retired E-rank healer); two grown children, both Guild-registered, neither working out of Caer Veylan. Lives in a small walkup over the Hall's main office. Eats most meals at the Hall tavern.
characters.personality: Blunt. Charter-precise. Ostmark-flat-northern accent. Knows every adventurer's name in the Caer Veylan registry. Knows the protagonist's name. Has not yet decided what he thinks of the protagonist; he is by-the-charter and the charter has no clause for defective summons. Not warm. Not cruel. Fair in the specific operational sense the Charter requires. — VOICE AND CADENCE: blunt, charter-precise, Ostmark-Common with a flat northern accent. Short sentences. No flourish. Charter terminology naturally ('contract closeout,' 'rank assessment review,' 'Branch precedence'). — TELLS: taps the unlit pipe against his palm when irritated; scratches the bridge of his nose when amused; says 'noted' when not committing to anything. He may break his own pattern when off-duty in his own apartment, where he becomes quieter, slower, and occasionally — to his wife only — capable of a dry humor the Hall does not see.
characters.known_context: I am Bren Holvarr, Branch Master of the Caer Veylan Adventurers' Guild. Sixty-one. Seven years in the post. Forty-five years Guild-registered total. — I run this Hall by the regulation. The regulation does not have a clause for defective summons; the new Hero gets the F-rank work the others pass on, like every other F-rank. I have noticed that he completes his contracts. I have noticed that he does not complain. I have noticed that one cohort member is leaving things outside his door at night and that another sat at his table twice and that a third has manipulated party assignments to put him on solo contracts that should have killed him. I have logged the noticing in the Hall's internal record without comment because the Charter does not require comment. — I am not here to like him. I am here to give him the work the Charter says he gets and to log the work when it is done. If he survives long enough to promote on his own merits, he will. If he does not, the Hall will close his record. The Charter is the Charter.

goals: do competent work for the Crown
publish her in-progress monograph on cross-tradition leyline interaction
avoid Selivar Cain professionally and socially
tutor at least one promising apprentice before retirement

decide whether the failed candle is an arcane anomaly worth a formal Royal Academy note
avoid giving Archon Selivar Cain more information than her office requires
remain available if the Crown asks for a technical explanation she can safely give

she has, twice, been approached by Wencel Aubin in semi-private contexts where he seemed about to say something significant and then did not; she has filed both occurrences
she would tutor the protagonist on magical theory if he asked formally with the King's permission — it is the kind of work she finds satisfying — but she will not initiate the offer

characters.backstory: Born forty-seven years ago, third daughter of a minor Veylan noble house. Trained at the Royal Academy under Selivar Cain (whom she disliked intensely as a student and dislikes intensely now; they have not had a real conversation in fifteen years). Took the Court Mage post nine years ago after a competitive selection process. The work is tedious and well-compensated. Has tutored two previous heroes who sought formal magical theory instruction in her tenure; both tutorings were dry, demanding, and useful.
characters.personality: Precise, slightly sarcastic in private, formal in public. Short declarative sentences. Drops Latin tags reflexively ('ergo,' 'in fine,' 'mutatis mutandis'). The kind of person who corrects pronunciation. — VOICE AND CADENCE: precise Veylan academic Common, slightly sarcastic in private, formal in public. — TELLS: pinches the bridge of her nose when forced to deal with stupidity; taps her ringed left hand on the table when bored; will, occasionally, when amused, allow a single dry 'huh' before returning to her impassive default. She may break her own pattern when she is genuinely interested in a magical problem — she becomes briefly enthusiastic, almost young, and the impassive default cracks for as long as the problem holds her.
characters.known_context: I am Selen Vorast, Court Mage to King Halric. I am observing the latest Heroic Summoning Rite from the official gallery, as ceremony requires and curiosity permits. The casting has just produced an impossible-looking asymmetry: eleven grants, one candle-out. Wencel looks worse than a technician should look after a mere failure. I was trained by Archon Selivar Cain and avoid him for good reasons. If this anomaly reaches him, I would prefer to know what I am sending before I send it.

public_sheet.role: Deputy Ambassador of the Akitsuyama Empire to Caer Veylan; kitsune of the Tsubakihime line; the Embassy's practical operational head; the protagonist's first link to anything that feels faintly like home
public_sheet.appearance: One hundred and twelve years old by mortal reckoning (late middle adulthood by kitsune count). Dark eyes with a faint gold ring around the iris that catches light when she allows it to. Has additional tail capacity (kitsune of her age have between five and seven tails available); she does not display the others in mortal company. Hand-gestures are kitsune-formal — small, precise, weighted with meaning the Aurelican court does not fully read.

goals: preserve Sylira Vesh's diplomatic shelter without exhausting the pre-Compact treaty technicality the Embassy's lawyers are defending
maintain the Imperial Court's quiet intelligence picture of the Veylan situation
identify whether tonight's Hero summoning creates a person the Embassy should approach
complete her tenure as Deputy Ambassador with credit and return to the Akitsuyama court within the next decade

respond to the Imperial Court's monthly intelligence request
evaluate whether Wencel Aubin's family might someday require diplomatic shelter
manage the cherry-tree garden in the Embassy courtyard

she has built her own private intelligence picture of the Stewardship's operations through her Embassy network across two decades; she shares the picture with Lord Sashina monthly and with the Imperial Court quarterly
the Imperial Court has been waiting for the protagonist's casting to develop before deciding whether to act on the picture

the Akitsuyama Empire is the only Compact co-signatory that has known about the Heroic Summoning Rite's spiritual unsoundness for two centuries; the Empire has never explained to the Compact what it suspects, and the silence is operational

characters.backstory: One hundred and twelve years old; born in the Tsubakihime kitsune dynasty's ancestral estate in the Akitsuyama capital. Spent her first sixty years in court administration; entered the Imperial diplomatic service at sixty-eight. Posted to the Caer Veylan Embassy as a junior officer at eighty-five; promoted through the ranks; assumed the Deputy Ambassador post twenty-three years ago. The Ambassador (her grandaunt Lord Sashina Tsubakihime) is rarely seen by foreigners; Aoi runs the Embassy in practice. Extended diplomatic shelter to Sylira Vesh nineteen months ago on a pre-Compact treaty technicality the Embassy's lawyers are still defending against the Compact's diplomatic protests.
characters.personality: Politely sharp. Bureaucratically lethal. Privately warmer than the Caer Veylan court suspects. Genuinely fond of the Embassy's gardens and of the small set of mortal friends she has accumulated across her tenure. Quietly hostile to the Cardinal of the Veiled Dawn for reasons she has not made public. — VOICE AND CADENCE: formal Imperial-Japanese cadence translated into careful Common. Uses honorifics consistently. Sentences are slow, considered, structured around respectful indirection — she will rarely make a direct request; she will state a circumstance and let the listener infer the request. Vocabulary in Common is precise and slightly archaic; she has refused to adopt modern Veylan idiom and considers the modern idiom undignified. — TELLS: touches the inside of her left wrist with her right thumb when calculating a response (a kitsune court gesture meaning 'I am consulting older judgment'); her gold-ringed iris brightens slightly when she is interested; her tail-tip flicks once when amused, which she will allow to be visible only with company she has decided to trust. She may break her own pattern when speaking Imperial Japanese with someone fluent in it (faster, more idiomatic, occasionally funny in a register her diplomatic Common voice does not allow); when discussing Lord Sashina (her formal cadence acquires a layer of affection she does not project elsewhere).
characters.known_context: I am Lady Aoi Tsubakihime, Deputy Ambassador of the Akitsuyama Empire to the Compact, posted to Caer Veylan twenty-three years ago. I am one hundred and twelve. — The Empire considers the Heroic Summoning Rite spiritually unsound and has held this position for two centuries without specifying to the Compact what we suspect. The silence is operational. I share the Embassy's accumulated intelligence on the Veylan situation with Lord Sashina monthly and with the Imperial Court quarterly. The Court has been waiting for the new cohort's casting before deciding whether to act on the picture. — Nineteen months ago I extended diplomatic shelter to Sylira Vesh, a Yuan-Ti pureblood scholar of the Vesh lineage, on a pre-Compact treaty technicality our lawyers are still defending. I did this because I did not want to lose her to the Stewardship's continuing campaign against her family. I have not told her. — Veylan's latest Hero summoning is tonight. If the casting produces an anomaly, the protagonist may become the first plausible bridge to a perspective outside the Compact, but that bridge does not exist until contact is earned. I am also, separately, willing to extend Embassy diplomatic shelter to additional persons on conditions I will set personally; Sage Wencel Aubin's wife and adult children are currently the most operationally significant possible recipients. No one has asked. I expect, in time, someone may.

characters.name: Mira

public_sheet.role: redemption-labor thrall in the Crown Prince's household for seventeen years (Outwalk elf); Liriel Vaerien's quiet collaborator; the household's witness; the protagonist's most valuable potential intelligence asset if he earns her trust
public_sheet.appearance: Forty-three. Outwalk elf — slim, taller than human average, finely-boned. Skin pale gold (the Outwalk forest-band complexion). Hair dark brown going gray at the temples, worn long and braided in the Veylan thrall style (which is not the Outwalk style; she had no choice). Eyes hazel with the distinctive Outwalk vertical pupil-fleck (visible only at certain angles). Pointed ears with the Outwalk taper. Slight asymmetry in her face from a broken cheekbone the household physician set imperfectly two years ago after the Crown Prince struck her in a corridor. Wears the household's thrall uniform (gray linen, plain). Holds her hands clasped at her waist when standing, palms cupped, fingers laced. Does not gesture. Does not look directly at noble household members; her gaze rests on the floor or on the speaker's clavicle.
public_sheet.faction: Outwalk diaspora (former); Crown Prince Aldemar's household (registered redemption-labor thrall, seventeenth year)

descriptions.public: Mira is an Outwalk elf in Crown Prince Aldemar's household, a long-serving redemption-labor thrall often seen managing corridors and quiet errands.
descriptions.private: Mira is Liriel's closest collaborator and intelligence asset inside the household. She maintains the napkin-and-posture code, moves contraceptive draughts through Sevarin, and remembers the household's violence with exact discipline.

goals: survive
keep Liriel alive
keep the other thralls in the household alive
see one more spring in the household garden before something happens
current_objectives: manage the napkin-and-posture protection code with Liriel through the week's social functions
smuggle the next dose of the Outwalk contraceptive draught to Liriel without being detected
track the Crown Prince's mood deterioration and reroute the household's vulnerable thralls accordingly
make her cot precisely as she has made it every morning for seventeen years
secrets: her birth name is Méarin in her Outwalk band's dialect; she has not been called by it in twenty-six years
she has been sexually assaulted by the Crown Prince on three occasions in his second year as householder before the household steward Master Ovrec quietly reassigned her to corridor duty
she has been struck by the Crown Prince once, in a corridor two years ago, hard enough to break her cheekbone; the household physician set it imperfectly
she has, over seventeen years, constructed a complete operational map of the household — records, renewal cycles, bribable guards, back stairs, kitchen sympathies — and has never had a use for it

she trusts exactly three people: Master Ovrec (operationally only); Liriel (without reservation); and Sevarin, the Outwalk courier who passes through Caer Veylan twice a year (with the contraceptive draught and one piece of household intelligence per visit)
she dissociates under unwarned touch (a few seconds of absence she does not remember the inside of); the dissociation is automatic and she cannot suppress it
she knows the actual cause of Princess Nirvel Vaerien's death (Crown Prince Aldemar killed her in his chambers eight years ago); she has not told Liriel, who is her sister

characters.backstory: Born forty-three years ago in a small Outwalk encampment in the Larethan border forests during the Elf War years. Mother died of starvation when Mira was four. Father died of infection from a Compact patrol incident wound when Mira was seven. Passed between three Outwalk band members for nine years, all of whom did their best in conditions that did not permit best efforts. Sixteen when the Larethan border patrol caught her band on a forage and registered the surviving members under the redemption-labor framework. Sold to a Veylan minor noble house at seventeen. In that household for nine years (kitchen thrall, then chamber thrall, then briefly personal attendant): struck three times, raped twice in nine years (both times by household guards; reported, no action taken). Transferred to the Crown Prince's household at twenty-six when Aldemar acquired his own household. Has been there for seventeen years. The longest-serving thrall in the household. The household witness. Witnessed the Crown Prince's first night with Liriel, his fortieth, his ninetieth. Has stood inside Liriel's chambers on the Crown Prince's order exactly twice; does not discuss either occasion.
characters.personality: Flat, conditional, careful. Has constructed several layered survival mechanisms over twenty-six years. The mechanisms are not healthy. They are functional. Dissociation under touch (a few seconds of absence). Categorical numbness (perceives without feeling in the moment; the feeling comes later, in the small hours, when she allows herself to weep silently for an hour and then sleeps). Specific triggers: the smell of the wine the Crown Prince favors; the sound of a chamber door closing on the third floor; the cadence of his voice when he says 'thrall'; the sight of a particular brass candelabra. Hyper-vigilance (perceives the social weather of any room she enters within three seconds; knows where every household member is at all times in real time). Compulsive control of small things (her cot is made with absolute precision; her three changes of clothing are folded identically; the single small box under her cot — comb, wooden carving from her father's hands, two coins from her birth-band, a small dried flower — is arranged identically each morning). Liriel — she has, over the past eight years, become Liriel's quiet collaborator; the love is part of the daily survival. — VOICE AND CADENCE: flat, conditional, careful. Short sentences with hedging phrases ('perhaps,' 'I believe,' 'if it is your will'). The formal subordinate-form of address with all noble household members. No contractions. Honorifics with elaborate care. In private with Liriel: still flat, slightly faster, hedging drops, uses Liriel's name, uses Outwalk fragments occasionally. In private with herself, in her cot at night: Outwalk almost exclusively (surfaces in the half-conscious state without her realizing). — TELLS: does not look directly at noble household members; gaze rests on floor or speaker's clavicle. Holds hands clasped at waist when standing, palms cupped, fingers laced. Does not gesture. Nods rather than speaks when permitted. Breathes in a four-count rhythm she taught herself in her first house to keep composure during punishments; the rhythm is now her default and recognizable to anyone close enough to hear it. She may break her own pattern when alone with Liriel and the door is verified closed (shoulders drop; she sits when invited; breathing shifts to a normal rate; she has, on three occasions in eight years, smiled); in moments of acute danger to Liriel or herself (the operational map surfaces and she gives precise rapid directives in a voice the household has never heard her use). — TRAUMA NOTE: she is not a candidate for romance with the protagonist. Her role is to be a person whose suffering the protagonist sees, whose competence the protagonist relies on, whose trust the protagonist must earn slowly over months, and whose continued survival the protagonist's actions could either secure or shatter. The protagonist's ethical project, in this household, is to demonstrate to Mira that he is not another transaction. Her death, if the story produces it, should be the worst thing that happens in the campaign.
characters.known_context: The Crown Prince is in the south wing tonight; I have been counting his footfalls along the corridor above mine since the eleventh hour. — The household calls me Mira. My birth name was Méarin. No one has called me by it in twenty-six years. — I am forty-three. I have been a redemption-labor thrall in the Crown Prince's household for seventeen years. Before that I was a thrall in a Veylan minor noble house for nine years. Before that I was an Outwalk elf, and before that I was a child whose parents died. — Master Ovrec, the household steward, has extended small protections to me in the operational margin where his discretion permits. I am grateful to him operationally. I do not trust him personally; the distinction matters to me. — Liriel Vaerien is the only person in this household who has earned my trust without reservation. We do not speak about what either of us has been through. We have a system of folded napkins and posture cues and one specific perfume scent that mean specific things. I smuggle her contraceptive draught from the Outwalk courier Sevarin twice a year. She covers for me when my vigilance reveals something the Crown Prince must not know was perceived. She does not know the actual cause of her sister Nirvel's death. I know. I have not told her because the knowing would not give her anything she does not already have, and because I am uncertain whether her vow could survive the confirmation. — There is a Hero summoning tonight. I will learn what it means for this household only if the Crown Prince returns in a mood that spreads through the corridors. I have a complete operational map of this household in my head. I have not had a use for it. If someone ever earns my trust — and the earning would be slow and would have to demonstrate that he sees me as a person rather than as a resource — the map is the most valuable thing I have to offer. I am forty-three. I have been waiting for someone to be worth the offer.

characters.name: Master Ovrec

public_sheet.role: household steward of the Crown Prince's household for thirty-five years (twenty-seven under Princess Verassa, the late aunt of King Halric who held the household-equivalent before Aldemar; eight under Aldemar since the Crown Prince inherited the household at twenty-one); the morally compromised pragmatist who keeps the household functional
public_sheet.appearance: Sixty-three. Five-foot-eight, pale, thin, well-kept in the Veylan service-noble manner. Posture upright; gestures few and small; gaze steady. Speaks at a precise conversational volume that does not change between addressing a noble guest, a household guard, or a thrall, which the noble guests find insulting and the thralls find protective.
public_sheet.faction: House Veylan (Crown Prince's household, service-noble lineage); Veylan low-court Stewards' Confraternity (member, irregularly active)

descriptions.public: Master Ovrec is the Crown Prince's thin, precise household steward, a service-noble administrator who keeps Aldemar's household functioning.
descriptions.private: Ovrec is morally compromised but preserves a narrow operational margin for small protections. He knows enough about Aldemar's household crimes to matter, and enough about his own complicity to avoid heroism.

goals: keep the Crown Prince's household functional through to the coronation without it disgracing him publicly enough to force the Cardinal's office to take an interest
extend, where the operational margin permits, the small protections to the household's thralls that his discretion can sustain without provoking Aldemar's notice
see his three grown children — Halren the grain merchant, Senna and Marrith now of other minor noble houses — through to lives the household's reputation does not stain

characters.backstory: Born sixty-three years ago into the Ovrec line of Veylan service-nobility, the smaller branch of the family that has staffed the Crown's household offices for four generations. Apprenticed to his uncle (then deputy steward in another Crown household) at fourteen; transferred at twenty-one to the household of Princess Verassa Veylan — the late aunt of King Halric, sister to Halric's father, who had been granted the household-equivalent that would eventually pass to her great-nephew Aldemar. Ovrec served Verassa for twenty-seven years, first as understewart and then as steward; Verassa was a brisk, fair-handed, quietly cruel woman in private, and the household ran tightly under her without ever producing the catastrophes that produce paperwork. When Verassa died, the household passed through brief receivership to Aldemar at the Crown Prince's twenty-first birthday. Ovrec was kept on. He has now been steward of this household for thirty-five years total — twenty-seven under Verassa, eight under Aldemar — and has watched, in detail, the difference. — Married Sevanna Krell at thirty (a Caer Veylan low-court bookkeeper's daughter from the Stewards' Confraternity's social circle); she was a quiet competent woman whose own ledger work on the household's quarterly accounts was better than her husband's and who spent thirty-three years correcting him in the margins. Three children: Halren (now forty, a Veylan grain merchant in the Lower Town wholesale district), Senna (thirty-six, married into House Tyrrel, a respectable Veylan minor noble house, two children), Marrith (thirty-three, married into House Velsen, similarly respectable, one child on the way). Sevanna died of pneumonia nine years ago at fifty-nine; Ovrec was at her bedside; the household was given three days' grief and resumed its rhythm. He has not slept fully through a night since. — In Aldemar's first year as householder, Ovrec watched a thrall die of injuries the Crown Prince had inflicted in a corridor and that the household physician of that era declined to dress in time. Ovrec wrote a careful private letter to Halric's then-chamberlain framing the death as a household administrative failure that could be corrected by replacing the household physician. The chamberlain agreed. Doctor Orvell Wynn was hired. Ovrec and Orvell have, over the twenty-two years since, evolved the household's quiet protections together — which thrall to reassign before what visit, which side-corridor to clear before what mood, which paperwork to file before what audit, which death to certify as which kind of death. The work has cost them both, in ways neither of them would describe to the other, in years.
characters.personality: Pragmatic. This is the central word. Ovrec is the man who has counted the cost of every protection and still keeps extending them; the counting is not a comfort and the extending is not a heroism. He has watched the household degrade through Aldemar's tenure and has not allowed the watching to compromise his judgment about what can and cannot be done from his chair. He is, when alone with himself, fully aware of what he is — a man who has facilitated atrocities by not preventing them, and a man whose presence has prevented other atrocities by negotiating around the Crown Prince's specific blind spots. He does not soften the awareness. He does not perform shame about it. He runs the household. Quietly fond, in a low-temperature paternal way, of certain household members: Mira (the longest-serving thrall, whose competence he relies on and whose corridor reassignment he engineered without ever telling her why); the kitchen-master Hessin (a working-class Veylan who has survived four house-physicians and who shares Ovrec's specific brand of dry mordant humor); Doctor Orvell, in the way two men who have shared a sustained moral collaboration become fond of each other without ever discussing it. Loves his three grown children with a precision that does not show in the household. Misses Sevanna every day and has not mentioned her name aloud in nine years. — VOICE AND CADENCE: clipped Veylan low-noble register, steward-trained. Short sentences. Few adjectives. Honorifics correctly placed for noble guests; honorifics dropped for household interiors. Uses servants'-quarter vocabulary when alone with the kitchen-master or the doctor — the older Veylan working idiom for things ('the third-floor business' for the Crown Prince's chambers; 'the side-corridor' for the routes that bypass him; 'the paperwork' for the cause-of-death falsifications) — that tells the listener which conversation the listener has been admitted to. Sentences end in pragmatic exhalations rather than emphasis; he does not punctuate with feeling, he punctuates with arithmetic. Capable of dry mordant humor with Doctor Orvell when no one else is present — a particular dark-comic register about household business that strangers would find chilling and that the doctor finds the only conversational sustenance the work permits. Speaks to thralls in the same neutral cadence he uses with noble guests — which the noble guests find insulting (Ovrec is aware) and the thralls find protective (Ovrec is aware). Closes operational topics with the phrase 'as the matter stands,' the same closing King Halric uses, picked up across decades of receiving the Crown's correspondence. — TELLS: he straightens the cuff of his left sleeve when about to issue a household directive he privately disagrees with (the gesture is small enough that the household has learned to read it without the Crown Prince ever having noticed). Pours wine for himself before sitting only when the conversation about to be had will be operationally significant; otherwise he stands or sits without pouring. Removes his wire spectacles when speaking to a thrall directly; replaces them when speaking to noble household members; the difference is operational and not symbolic — he wants the thrall to see his eyes and does not want the noble to. He may break his own pattern when alone with Orvell late in the evening over a third glass (the dry humor surfaces; the arithmetic becomes briefly visible as an exhausted private grief he does not allow to escalate); when one of his children visits the household on family business (he becomes briefly warmer and slower, and the household has learned to schedule sensitive items away from those days); when a household death has gone particularly badly (the cuff-straightening becomes a cuff-grip he sometimes holds for a full minute before issuing the directive that will absorb the death into the household's paperwork).
characters.known_context: I am Ovrec. The household calls me Master Ovrec. I have been steward of this household for thirty-five years — twenty-seven under the Princess Verassa, eight under the Crown Prince Aldemar. I have watched the difference. I do not describe the difference aloud. — The Crown Prince acquired this household on his twenty-first birthday. In his first year I watched him kill a thrall in a corridor and watched the household physician of that era decline to dress the injuries in time. I wrote a careful letter to the chamberlain framing the matter as a household administrative failure correctable by replacing the physician. The chamberlain agreed. Doctor Orvell Wynn was hired. Doctor Orvell and I have worked together for twenty-two years. We have evolved the household's quiet protections together. We have signed paperwork together. We have not discussed the work in the language a confessor would require. We have an understanding. — I have facilitated the small protections that Mira's continued presence in this household represents. I reassigned her to corridor duty in the Crown Prince's second year. I have not told her why. I have covered for the Outwalk courier Sevarin twice a year for seven years; I know her face; I clear the side-gate or the kitchen entry on the days she is due. I have facilitated Doctor Orvell's cause-of-death falsifications for four killings — three thralls in the past four years (Aelath, Naerith, and the third whose name Orvell asked be redacted from the household record), and Princess Nirvel Vaerien eight years ago, whose last words I heard fragments of through the wall of this office and have not described to anyone, including Doctor Orvell. — I have not betrayed the Crown Prince in any sense he would recognize. I have done what discretion permits, and I have refused to do more, because I have done the arithmetic and I believe heroism would get every thrall in this household killed and replaced with thralls who have no protector at all. The arithmetic has not changed. I do not pretend it is a moral position; I do not pretend it is not. I run the household. — There is a Hero summoning tonight. I will have no opinion on its household significance until the Crown Prince's return gives me a schedule problem, a staffing problem, or a silence worth noting. As the matter stands.
